name: Inductive Thermal Lance
description:
The Inductive Thermal Lance is a heavy close-combat weapon produced by Palladian Construction, originally developed as a field tool for emergency structural cutting in collapsed building scenarios. The ITL-5 consists of a 90-centimeter reinforced handle assembly connected to a 40-centimeter ferrous core lance tip surrounded by a tight helical induction coil. When powered, the coil generates a rapidly alternating magnetic field that induces eddy currents directly within the ferrous tip, heating it to operational temperature — approximately 900 degrees Celsius — within four seconds, without any external flame or combustion. The tip glows a deep amber-orange at operating temperature and maintains heat continuously while powered.

The transition from construction tool to weapon was, by most accounts, inevitable given the ITL-5's field profile. Palladian Construction workers in contested infrastructure zones began carrying them as combination tools and deterrents, and the design's robustness — built to function in debris fields, flooded basements, and chemically contaminated environments — made it a natural fit for the kinds of chaotic close-quarters scenarios common in GLMZ's lower districts. Palladian has never officially marketed the ITL-5 as a weapon, but their industrial sales division has been notably uninterested in investigating end-user applications, and modified versions with sharpened tips and shortened handles have been documented in the hands of non-construction personnel for years.

The ITL-5's combat profile is defined by its ability to defeat armor through thermal transfer rather than kinetic force. Against standard ballistic plate, the lance tip burns through the outer layer within seconds of sustained contact, defeating the material's protective properties before mechanical penetration is attempted. Against biological targets, the cauterizing effect of the weapon simultaneously wounds and seals — a grim feature that operators in extended engagements have described as 'efficient,' as it reduces the user's risk of exposure to target blood.
specifications:
total length: 130 cm (handle + lance)
lance tip material: High-carbon ferrous alloy, hardened
operating temperature: 900°C sustained at full power
heat up time: 4 seconds to operational temperature
power source: Backpack-mounted high-capacity cell, 40-minute continuous operation; handle-integrated cell available (12-minute operation)
weight: 3.8 kg with handle cell
cooling time: 90 seconds from power-off to safe handling
induction coil material: Wound copper-beryllium alloy, shielded
tactical_use: In construction and emergency response contexts, the ITL-5 is used for cutting through rebar, locked structural panels, and collapsed framework. In combat, operators use sustained contact pressure to defeat armor before pushing through, a technique that requires the user to maintain engagement range — risky, but devastatingly effective against opponents who rely on hardened protection. The lance's length provides standoff advantage against knife-range weapons, and its weight makes it effective as a bludgeoning implement even when unpowered. Experienced operators carry it unpowered until engagement is confirmed, activating it mid-approach to deny opponents preparation time. The 90-second cooling delay after shutdown is a known vulnerability — an operator who powers down cannot safely stow or conceal the weapon quickly.
cultural_context: In GLMZ's construction worker communities, carrying an ITL-5 is a normalized part of working in contested infrastructure zones where labor disputes can turn violent and rival crews compete over demolition contracts. The weapon has consequently become associated with organized labor's harder edges — union enforcers and territorial crew bosses are frequently depicted carrying them in the city's underground press. In the upper districts, the ITL-5 is viewed as a working-class weapon, too crude and industrial for corporate security tastes, which has paradoxically made it a symbol of working-district identity. Modified 'dueling' versions with decorative coil wrapping and sharpened tips are carried by gang leadership in the Palladian Construction service districts as an explicit territorial symbol.
known_users: Palladian Construction emergency response and field crews
Organized labor enforcers in the construction sector
Gang leadership in Palladian service districts
Scavengers and salvage operators working contested demolition zones
Drevko Mass, union organizer and documented ITL-5 duelist
story_hooks: A series of structural fires in a contested district have been started using ITL-5 units — the burns are too precise for accident, and the pattern suggests someone is systematically destroying buildings to clear land for a construction bid. Palladian Construction is a likely beneficiary.

A modified ITL-5 with an induction coil rated far above the standard ceiling has been used in an attack — it reached temperatures that melted through reinforced vault-grade material. Someone has cracked Palladian's design and is manufacturing a version the original engineers say shouldn't be possible.

A players' contact in the construction labor movement has been arrested on weapon charges — an ITL-5 found at a crime scene has been traced to their registered license. They claim it was stolen three weeks ago. Finding the actual user means navigating both corporate security and labor union politics.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutal marriage of industrial tool and close-combat weapon — a heavy, purposeful shaft that tapers to a glowing amber tip when activated. The overall silhouette reads as a polearm crossed with construction equipment: brutalist, overbuilt, uncompromising. At rest, it's a dull industrial object; powered, it becomes a beacon of lethal heat.
physical_description.dimensions: Total length: 130 cm (handle 90 cm, lance tip 40 cm). Shaft diameter: 4.2 cm. Tip width at widest point: 3.8 cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Hefty and purposeful — 3.8 kg demands commitment from the user, front-weighted toward the tip. Balanced for sustained contact pressure rather than quick strikes. Feels like swinging concentrated intention.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced steel shaft with hardened high-carbon ferrous alloy lance tip. Copper-beryllium induction coil wound tightly around the tip section, shielded with low-conduction polymer casing.
physical_description.finish: Industrial matte black powder coat on the handle section, showing practical wear at grip zones. The ferrous tip itself has a brushed metallic finish that oxidizes to dull charcoal when powered down; when active, the amber glow overwhelms surface detail. Visible heat distortion around the coil housing during operation.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal-black steel body with burnt orange/amber tip when unpowered (oxidized ferrous surface). When activated: deep glowing amber-orange radiating from the tip, with subtle heat shimmer visible along the coil housing. Accent color: industrial yellow warning striping on the handle near the grip.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer grip section with shallow vertical ridges for purchase, rated for wet/contaminated conditions. Bare steel control collar at mid-shaft where the operator's guide hand sits. Slight tackiness to the rubber from age and handling.
distinctive_features: Tightly wound copper-beryllium coil visible beneath translucent polymer shielding around the tip section — geometric grid pattern of windings
Deep recessed activation button on the shaft, lever-style, requiring thumb pressure and intentional contact
Heat exhaust vents along the coil housing, arranged in asymmetrical staggered rows
Status indicator LED (green/red) embedded in the top of the grip collar, visible only from above
Ferrous tip has a pronounced edge — sharpened but not knife-like, more of a cutting chisel than blade
Faint PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION stamp on the handle, partially worn
Discoloration around the base of the tip section from repeated heating cycles
Cable conduit running along the shaft toward the backpack mount interface (when backpack cell used)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: PALLADIAN CONSTRUCTION logo — a stylized angular 'P' — stamped on the upper handle section, approximately 12 cm from the grip. Model designation 'ITL-5' embossed below. Serial number etched into a recessed plate on the mid-shaft (often obfuscated on field units). Regulatory compliance markings in microscopic text near the activation button.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained industrial tool showing practical use. No deep battle scarring, but visible oxidation staining around the tip from repeated thermal cycles. Grip rubber shows polished wear patterns from gloved operation. Minor dents in the matte black shaft — the result of being used as a prying lever. Some units show field-applied tape or cord wrapping at the grip. The ferrous tip may show micro-fracturing or slight warping on units pushed beyond rated operational parameters.
